threads.body:
The new "USER" keyword rule only handles operation targets and never falls back to `operation.handleIdentifier()` when `expectingOperationTarget()` is false. This changes parsing behavior for statements where an identifier is literally `user` (e.g., `SELECT * FROM user`, `ALTER TABLE user ...`), which previously went through the `{IDENTIFIER}` rule and could be captured as a table/procedure/etc. Consider handling `USER` the same way as other reserved words (e.g., include it in the existing `"TABLE" | "INDEX" | ...` rule) so it acts as an identifier when not in the DDL-target position.

This issue also appears on line 512 of the same file.

threads.body:
The new "USER" keyword rule does not call `cancelPendingSubqueryIfNeeded()` or `operation.handleIdentifier()` when `expectingOperationTarget()` is false. This can break query-summary extraction when an identifier is literally `user` (e.g., table named `user`) and can also interfere with the pending-subquery heuristic. Consider folding `USER` into the existing reserved-word handler (`"TABLE" | "INDEX" | ...`) so it behaves like other reserved words in non-target positions.

This issue also appears on line 1033 of the same file.

threads.body: [Bug] `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterSensitivePhrase()` only exempts operations that extend `DmlOperation`. In this lexer, several data-modifying statements (e.g., REPLACE, VALUES) are modeled as `Operation`, so a column/table identifier named `password` in those statements will hit the `"PASSWORD"` rule and incorrectly truncate/redact the rest of the statement. Consider classifying all DML-like operations as `DmlOperation` (or broadening the predicate) so normal identifier usage doesn’t trigger sensitive-phrase redaction.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/9722f8921b6.

The sanitizer now defaults operations to not truncating after sensitive phrases; only DDL/admin operations that can contain password clauses opt into that behavior.

threads.body: [Bug] The `"PASSWORD"` token rule redacts/truncates the remainder whenever `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterSensitivePhrase()` is true, even when `PASSWORD` is being used as an identifier (e.g., table/database name) rather than a secret clause. This can produce incorrect sanitized SQL by inserting an extra `?` and stopping early (for example, `TRUNCATE TABLE password` would become `TRUNCATE TABLE password ?`). Consider gating the truncation on context that indicates a secret clause (or detect when the token was consumed as an identifier and avoid redaction in that case).

threads.body: [Bug] The expected query summaries for the `ALTER USER ...` sensitive cases omit the username, but the summary sanitizer’s DDL logic appends the first identifier after the operation target (so `ALTER USER user ...` will summarize as `ALTER USER user`). Either update these expectations to include the identifier (consistent with `CREATE USER new_user ...`) or adjust the sanitizer to intentionally skip capturing identifiers for `ALTER USER` if that’s the desired behavior.

threads.body: [Bug] The `"PASSWORD"` token rule will truncate/redact the remainder for any non-DML operation (including `NoOp` when the statement type isn’t recognized). This means `PASSWORD` used as an identifier (e.g., table/database name in an unrecognized statement like `TRUNCATE TABLE password`) will be transformed into `... password ?` and stop scanning. Consider gating the truncation on context that indicates a secret clause, or at least avoid adding the trailing `?`/YYEOF when `PASSWORD` is functioning as an identifier.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/9722f8921b6.

The non-summary sanitizer now only truncates after PASSWORD/IDENTIFIED BY in explicit sensitive-clause contexts, so identifier uses such as TRUNCATE TABLE password are preserved.

threads.body: In the non-summary sanitizer, the `"GRANT" | "VALIDATE" | "CHECK" | "EXPORT" | "RECOVER"` rule unconditionally enables `sensitivePhraseSanitizationAllowed` whenever these keywords appear outside comments. If one of these tokens is used as an identifier inside a normal DML statement (similar to the existing `SELECT connect ...` control case), it can wrongly enable sensitive-phrase truncation later in the same statement (e.g., `SELECT grant, password FROM users` would truncate at `PASSWORD`). Consider guarding this flag the same way as the `CONNECT` rule (e.g., only enable when `operation == NoOp.INSTANCE` / at statement start), or otherwise tie it to an explicit admin-statement context instead of any occurrence of the keyword.

replies.body: Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/18754/commits/a54cf738223. The non-summary admin keyword rule now only enables sensitive-phrase sanitization when the keyword starts the statement (`operation == NoOp.INSTANCE`), and I added the `SELECT grant, password FROM users` regression case.

threads.body: `sensitivePhraseSanitizationAllowed` is a sticky flag that is never cleared. For multi-statement SQL (the tests cover semicolons in `simplifyArgs()`), a statement that starts with an admin keyword (e.g., `GRANT ...; SELECT password FROM users`) will enable this flag for the whole input, causing the later `PASSWORD` identifier in a subsequent statement to trigger `YYEOF` truncation/redaction incorrectly. Consider scoping the flag to a single statement by clearing it when a statement terminator (`;`) is encountered outside comments (without resetting `operation`, since old-semconv extraction intentionally sticks to the first statement), or otherwise resetting it when starting a new statement context.

threads.body: `Grant` now extends `SensitivePhraseOperation`, which makes any occurrence of the `PASSWORD` token inside a GRANT statement trigger `YYEOF` truncation in the `"PASSWORD"` rule (since `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterSensitivePhrase()` becomes true). This causes incorrect sanitization for GRANTs on objects literally named `password` (e.g., `GRANT SELECT ON password TO admin` would be truncated to `... password ?`). Consider scoping sensitive-phrase truncation for GRANT to `IDENTIFIED BY` only (or otherwise special-casing the PASSWORD rule so identifier uses of `password` in GRANT statements don’t truncate the remainder).

threads.body: Including `"GRANT"` in the admin-keyword rule enables `sensitivePhraseSanitizationAllowed` for the entire statement whenever `GRANT` starts the SQL. This means an identifier named `password` later in the same GRANT (e.g., `GRANT SELECT ON password TO admin`) will match the `"PASSWORD"` token rule and incorrectly trigger remainder truncation (`... password ?`). Consider separating “allow IDENTIFIED BY truncation” from “allow PASSWORD truncation”, or otherwise ensuring GRANT only truncates on `IDENTIFIED BY` and not on the standalone `PASSWORD` token.

threads.body: `PASSWORD` is always treated as the start of a sensitive clause for DDL/admin operations (via `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterPassword()`), even when it appears in the position where an identifier is expected. For example, `CREATE USER password PASSWORD secret` or `CREATE DATABASE password ...` will hit this rule on the object name `password` and truncate early (`... password ?`) before reaching the real password clause. Consider detecting when `PASSWORD` is being used as the first identifier after a DDL operation target (or otherwise when the current token is being consumed as the captured identifier) and skipping the remainder-redaction in that case, so later `PASSWORD` clauses can still be redacted correctly.

threads.body: The `PASSWORD` keyword is redacted via `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterPassword()` immediately after calling `operation.handleIdentifier()`. If the identifier being captured is literally `password` (e.g., `CREATE USER password PASSWORD ...` / `CREATE DATABASE password ...`), this rule will treat the object name as a sensitive clause and stop scanning early, producing incorrect sanitized SQL and an incomplete summary. Consider special-casing `PASSWORD` when it occurs in the “first identifier after DDL target” position so it can be captured as an identifier without triggering remainder redaction; only subsequent `PASSWORD` occurrences (actual clauses) should truncate.

threads.body: `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterIdentifiedBy()` currently falls back to `operation.shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterPassword()`, which makes IDENTIFIED BY sanitization implicitly tied to the PASSWORD behavior. This looks like a copy/paste oversight and prevents operation-specific IDENTIFIED BY behavior (the summary sanitizer already has a dedicated `shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterIdentifiedBy()` hook, e.g., for GRANT). Consider adding `Operation.shouldSanitizeRemainderAfterIdentifiedBy()` in this lexer too and delegating to it here to keep the two sanitizers consistent and easier to evolve safely.
